newsitem.title: GERMANY: German post staff protest over end of monopoly.
newsitem.headline: German post staff protest over end of monopoly.

text.p: Around 16,000 German postal workers took part in stoppages and protests against a new law seeking to remove the German post office's 100-year-old-plus monopoly, the German postal trade union said on Friday.

The action comes as speculation mounts that the German postal market will be freed up to competition earlier and more completely than previously expected because of pressure from some politicians within the Bonn coalition.

The Deutsche Postgewerkschaft (DPG) union said workers at some 80 sorting centres across Germany had participated in stoppages starting with the late shift on Thursday and leading to some disruption of letter distribution.
Rallies had also taken place outside regional offices of the Christian Democrat and Free Democrat (FDP) Bonn coalition partners, the DPG said.

Government sources have said that opposition from FDP politicians will likely mean that earlier plans by post minister Wolfgang Boetsch to grant the post office a five-year exclusive operator licence will not be approved.

The DPG fears that the new postal law, due to be agreed next week, will instead open the market up to "cherry-picking", in which rival operators will from the end of this year be able to operate in only the most lucrative parts of the market.
It said such a move could put tens of thousands of existing post office jobs at risk.
DPG wants a postal law that would guarantee a high degree of universal service and allow the Post AG post office sufficient scope to finance its general postal services.
